set.body:
Source: docs/plans/2026-07-30-pre-1.0-correctness-and-architecture.md, the verified response to the 2026-07-29 external review (eight release-blocking issue groups plus user-surface, assurance, and compatibility findings).

Verification boundary (phase-0-discipline, clean, HEAD 95faeb5):
- sbt -batch test => 305 tests, 0 failed, 28 s, Scala 3.7.4. No files changed.
- Every claim carried by a child bead is cited file:line and was checked against source.
- Not performed: real Slurm site contact, 3.3.8/3.8.4 builds, fault injection.
The suite passing is not evidence against these findings. Every Phase A defect is invisible to the current suite by construction, because the tests encode the same assumptions the code does.

Objective:
Reach a defensible 0.1.0 by closing the reachable correctness holes first, settling the launch/result architecture second, and cutting the compatibility baseline only after all public-shape churn is done.

Sequence: A + B (parallel) -> C -> D -> E -> F -> G

Why this order (the substance of this epic):
The review's own P0->P3 ordering, followed literally, encodes the wire three times. The state-model redesign touches 52 SlurmState references in protocol/AgentDomainJson.scala; then P7.2 swaps the byte representation underneath those codecs; then P6f.12 hand-writes every codec again.

EPIC P7 established "representation (P7.2) before hand-writing codecs (P6f.12)". The correct generalization is that public SHAPE settles first too, and the LaunchSpec/PreparedJob split (D1/D2) is a larger shape change than P7.2 is a representation change.

The resolution is to split the P0 findings by whether they change public shape:
- Phase A closes every reachable hang and false-certainty bug with semantics-only changes, so none of that work is redone later.
- Phase D lands every structural redesign in one API-churn window, immediately before codec ownership.
- Phase B (laws, -Werror) runs early because it is the safety net UNDER Phase D. The review placed it at P2, after all architecture, which inverts its purpose.

Relationship to EPIC P7 (bd-01KYNA41P38JDSB9PVH5WS8M2D):
This epic supersedes P7's SEQUENCING only. All five of P7's structural gaps survive intact: Phase E is P7.3/P7.2/P6f.12/P7.4, Phase F is P7.6/P6f.18, and P7.1/P6f.5a/P6f.33a feed Phase G4. No P7 bead is obsoleted; several gain new blockers from Phase D. P7.5 is absorbed by P8.D5, which is strictly larger.

Completion rule:
Held to the P6f.28-P6f.39 standard: every fix ships with a test demonstrated RED against the parent commit. A green suite alone does not close a Phase A bead.

Explicitly out of scope: the Site layer; SSH protocol multiplexing (ADR 0003 one-process-per-request stands); any production-support claim before two real sites qualify (G4).

Open decisions recorded in the plan, not yet settled by the owner:
1. Supersede vs. coexist with P7 (this epic assumes supersede-sequencing-only).
2. Release target: 0.1.0 experimental at Phase F, 1.0 after G4.
3. Wire compatibility for A2/A5: no tags and nothing published, so no migration story is believed necessary. Confirm nothing is already persisted in a user's store.
4. Federation: D4 declares cross-cluster routing unsupported for v1. Confirm no near-term site needs -M.
5. Phase A branch policy: whether A1-A4 ship as a pre-baseline tag or wait for Phase F.
set.title: EPIC P8: Pre-1.0 correctness, architecture, and assurance
